name: A Centrifugal Casting Rig Using Rotation for Mould Filling in Orbit: Rotational Energy, Artificial-Gravity and Thermal Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for cylindrical bushings, ring gears and axisymmetric housings in orbit, using molten aluminium-silicon alloy from a resistance melter. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a mould mounted at the rim of a 1.2 metre rotor is spun so that centrifugal acceleration, rather than gravity, drives molten metal outward and holds it against the mould wall while it freezes.

name: A Chemical Vapour Deposition Coater for Orbital Hardening of Tools and Optics: Precursor, Reaction-Rate and Energy Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for titanium-nitride-coated tools, wear surfaces and optical components in orbit, using titanium tetrachloride, nitrogen and hydrogen precursor gases. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: precursor gases react at a heated substrate surface and deposit a ceramic film a few micrometres thick, molecule by molecule.

name: A Cold-Spray Deposition Unit for Orbital Repair and Coating of Aluminium Structures: Gas, Kinetic-Energy and Throughput Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for restored sealing faces, conductive coatings and repaired panels in orbit, using aluminium and copper powder, 15-45 micrometre grade. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: heated nitrogen expands through a de Laval nozzle to supersonic speed and carries powder particles that bond on impact by severe plastic deformation, without ever melting.

name: A Contactless Electromagnetic Levitation Foundry for Orbital Casting of Nickel Superalloy Parts: Induction, Radiation and Energy Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for small turbine-grade castings and single-crystal seed stock in orbit, using pre-alloyed nickel superalloy spheres, 40 gram charge. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a radio-frequency coil both levitates and inductively heats a free-floating metal charge, which melts without touching any crucible and therefore without crucible contamination.

name: A Cryogenic Boiloff Reliquefier for Orbital Propellant Depots: Heat-Leak, Carnot and Refrigeration-Power Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for reliquefied propellant returned to the depot tanks, with zero routine venting in orbit, using boiloff vapour from liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen depot tanks. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a closed-cycle helium refrigerator intercepts boiloff vapour from depot tanks and condenses it back to liquid, replacing the usual practice of venting or burning off the excess.

name: A Fibre-Laser Powder-Bed Fusion Cell for Orbital Production of Aluminium Components: Optical, Energy and Radiator Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for aluminium heat-exchanger cores and lightweight structural shells in orbit, using AlSi10Mg powder, 20-63 micrometre grade. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a 1 kilowatt ytterbium fibre laser, delivered through a galvanometer scanner, melts successive 40 micrometre layers of aluminium powder inside a nitrogen-lean, low-pressure chamber.

name: A Friction-Stir Additive Machine for Orbital Fabrication of Large Aluminium Plates: Torque, Travel and Energy Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for large flat structural plates and tank wall sections too wide for powder beds in orbit, using aluminium 2219 plate feedstock and shoulder stock. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a rotating non-consumable tool plunges into stacked plate and traverses, plasticising and forging the metal in the solid state as it goes, so a large plate is built by stirring rather than melting.

name: A Loop-Heat-Pipe and Deployable Radiator System for Thermal Control of Orbital Production Equipment: Capillary, Radiative and Mass Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for steady equipment temperatures held within a 20 kelvin band during production cycles in orbit, using waste heat from co-located production equipment, ammonia working fluid. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: ammonia loop heat pipes collect waste heat from production equipment and carry it, without pumps, to deployable radiator panels, where it is radiated to space.

name: A Molten-Salt Electrolysis Recycler for Orbital Recovery of Aluminium from Scrap: Cell Voltage, Faraday and Thermal Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for recovered aluminium metal and reusable alloying fractions in orbit, using aluminium scrap, failed printed parts and machining swarf in a calcium chloride bath. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: scrap aluminium and mixed light-alloy waste are dissolved and re-won electrochemically in a molten calcium chloride bath near 1150 kelvin, following the solid-oxide reduction route demonstrated terrestrially for metal recycling.

name: A Plasma Pyrolysis Recycler for Orbital Recovery of Hydrocarbons from Polymer Waste: Plasma Enthalpy, Yield and Energy Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for hydrogen-rich gas, carbon black and a condensable hydrocarbon fraction in orbit, using mixed polyethylene and packaging waste from station operations. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a direct-current plasma torch raises shredded polymer waste to about 3000 kelvin in an oxygen-free reactor, breaking long chains into a hydrogen-rich gas and solid carbon rather than burning them.

name: A Solar-Concentrator Sintering Furnace for Orbital Production from Metal Powder: Collection Area, Thermal and Throughput Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for sintered gears, filters and porous flow elements in orbit, using gas-atomised steel and nickel powder. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a deployable parabolic concentrator collects sunlight and focuses it onto a small rotating furnace cavity, raising powder compacts to sintering temperature without any electrical heating element.

name: A Wire-Arc Additive Machine for Orbital Fabrication of Steel Frames: Arc Power, Deposition and Shielding Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for steel frame nodes, trunnion blocks and other bulky low-precision structure in orbit, using 1.2 millimetre steel welding wire on spools. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a gas-metal arc struck from the feed wire itself deposits steel bead by bead into near-net shapes.

name: An Electron-Beam Melting Printer for Orbital Production of Titanium Components: Energy, Thermal and Mass Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for titanium brackets, fittings and pressure housings in orbit, using Ti-6Al-4V powder, 45-106 micrometre grade. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a focused electron beam, accelerated through 60 kilovolts and magnetically deflected, scans a preheated powder bed in vacuum and fully melts each layer.

name: An Inchworm Robotic Assembler for Orbital Construction of a 100-Metre Truss: Joint Energy, Traverse and Schedule Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for a 100 metre backbone truss for antennas, radiators and solar arrays in orbit, using pre-manufactured carbon-composite struts and node fittings launched as a kit. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a two-ended inchworm robot walks along the truss it is building, alternately gripping with each end, placing struts from a carried magazine and driving each joint home, so the structure itself is the robot's railway and no free-flying translation is needed for most operations.

name: An Inflatable and Ultraviolet-Rigidised Shell System for Orbital Workshops: Gas, Curing and Surface-Area Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for a rigid workshop shell 8 metres in diameter for housing production equipment in orbit, using glass-fibre laminate impregnated with ultraviolet-curing resin, packed flat. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a folded laminate shell is inflated with a small gas charge to its working shape and then exposed, panel by panel, to concentrated solar ultraviolet, which polymerises the resin and converts the soft shell into a rigid structure.

name: An Orbital Electroforming System for Nickel Reflector Shells and Waveguides: Faraday-Law, Power and Solution-Mass Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for thin nickel reflector shells, waveguide sections and precision replication moulds in orbit, using nickel sulfamate electrolyte and soluble nickel anodes. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: nickel ions are reduced onto a rotating mandrel from a temperature-controlled sulfamate bath, building a stress-free shell atom by atom at a rate fixed by Faraday's law.

name: An Ultrasonic Foil Consolidation Machine for Orbital Production of Embedded-Sensor Panels: Acoustic Power, Energy and Mass Budgets
territory: In-Space Manufacturing, Assembly and Recycling Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a computed design study, SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED, for honeycomb-core panels with embedded fibre-optic and thermocouple sensors in orbit, using aluminium 6061 foil tape, 150 micrometre thick. The operating principle is distinct from neighbouring production methods: a rolling sonotrode vibrating at 20 kilohertz welds metal foil tape layer by layer under a steady normal force, a solid-state process whose peak temperature stays well below melting.

name: A Buried Regolith Sensible-Heat Store Carrying Habitat Heat Through the Lunar Night
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a buried regolith sensible-heat store that carries a 354-hour lunar night heating load of 10 kilowatts: allowing for losses, the store must hold 4.4 megawatt-hours of heat, requiring 99.6 tonnes of regolith swung through 200 kelvin, a volume of 66 cubic metres equivalent to a cube 4.0 metres on a side. Sizing follows from computed thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: A Fission Surface Power Unit with Free-Piston Stirling Conversion Sized from Its Waste-Heat Budget
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a fission surface power unit delivering 40.0 kilowatts of electricity through free-piston Stirling conversion at an efficiency of 0.25, requiring 160 kilowatts of reactor thermal power and rejecting 120 kilowatts of waste heat through a radiator at 400 kelvin with an area of 91.9 square metres. Uranium-235 consumption is 0.06 kilograms per year, or 0.6 kilograms over a ten-year operating life.

name: A Loop Heat Pipe Radiator Array Rejecting Habitat Waste Heat Across the Day-Night Cycle
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a loop heat pipe radiator array rejecting 50.0 kilowatts of habitat waste heat from panels at 310 kelvin: each square metre radiates 482 watts, so the array needs 104 square metres before margin and 130 square metres with the stated design margin, served by 34 transport loops at the stated per-loop capacity. Sizing follows from computed thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: A Regenerative Hydrogen-Oxygen Fuel Cell System Carrying a Lunar Outpost Through the Night
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a regenerative hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell system carrying a 15 kilowatt outpost load through the 354 hour night: night energy is 5 megawatt-hours, requiring 245 kilograms of hydrogen and 1959 kilograms of oxygen cycling through 2204 kilograms of water, a daytime electrical input of 14 megawatt-hours at a round-trip efficiency of 38 percent, and hydrogen storage volume of 6.1 cubic metres at the stated density. Sizing follows from computed energy budgets derived in the study.

name: A Vapour-Compression Heat Pump Drawing on Subsurface Warmth for Lunar Night Habitat Heating
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a vapour-compression heat pump delivering 12 kilowatts of habitat heat through the lunar night from a subsurface source at 240 kelvin: the Carnot coefficient of performance is 5.36, the working coefficient at the stated second-law efficiency is 2.41, electrical demand is 4.97 kilowatts and ground extraction is 7.0 kilowatts. Sizing follows from computed thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: A Water-Ice Phase-Change Buffer Smoothing Peak Thermal Loads at a Lunar Habitat
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a water-ice phase-change buffer that shaves an 8 kilowatt thermal peak lasting 6 hours: the buffer must absorb 173 megajoules, requiring 0.52 tonnes of ice with a volume of 0.57 cubic metres at the stated utilisation. Sizing follows from computed thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: An Electrostatic Precipitator Airlock Stage for Suit and Equipment Dust Removal
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes an electrostatic precipitator stage for a habitat airlock: at the stated migration velocity, plate area and flow, collection efficiency is 99.33 percent, reducing a stated 50 gram incoming dust load per entry to a residual of 0.337 grams. Sizing follows from computed budgets derived in the study.

name: An Elevated Photovoltaic Tower at a Polar Illuminated Ridge Supplying Near-Continuous Power
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes an elevated photovoltaic tower at a polar illuminated ridge: a 300 square metre array at the stated tower illumination fraction averages 71.4 kilowatts and yields 625 megawatt-hours per year, against 405 megawatt-hours at ground level at the stated ground fraction, a gain of 221 megawatt-hours per year. Sizing follows from computed energy budgets derived in the study.

name: Concentrated Solar Thermophotovoltaic Power for a Lunar Daytime Work Site
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes a concentrated solar thermophotovoltaic system delivering 20.0 kilowatts of daytime electricity: with a cell conversion fraction of 0.22 the emitter must absorb 90.9 kilowatts, collected through a concentrator aperture of 83.5 square metres onto an emitter of 0.32 square metres at 1500 kelvin, a concentration ratio near 264, for an overall sunlight-to-electricity efficiency of 17.6 percent. Sizing follows from computed energy budgets derived in the study.

name: Electrodynamic Dust Shielding for Solar Arrays and Radiator Surfaces
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes electrodynamic dust shielding for a 200 square metre solar array: dust derating at the stated level would cost 12.5 kilowatts of output, while the shield draws an average of 100 watts at the stated duty cycle, a net protection of 12.4 kilowatts and a benefit ratio near 125. Sizing follows from computed energy budgets derived in the study.

name: Inflatable Formwork with a Regolith-Covered Arch for Rapid Habitat Shielding Construction
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes inflatable-formwork construction of a regolith-covered arch bay of 8 metre span and 12 metre length: the arch presents 151 square metres, a 1 metre cover requires 151 cubic metres, about 226 tonnes, of regolith, and the cover weight load of 2430 pascals under lunar gravity sits within the stated form pressure during placement. Sizing follows from computed regolith budgets derived in the study.

name: Microwave-Sintered Regolith Bricks Assembled into a Shielding Vault
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes microwave-sintered regolith brick production for a hemispherical shielding vault of 4 metre radius: each brick needs 18.3 megajoules at the stated coupling efficiency, the vault needs 1257 bricks, and total production energy is 23.0 gigajoules, about 128 hours at 50 kilowatts of microwave power. Brick mass is 12.0 kilograms.

name: Passive Radiative Cooling Panels for Lunar Daytime Equipment Temperature Control
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes passive radiative cooling panels operating in lunar daylight: a panel at 300 kelvin emits 436 watts per square metre, absorbs 109 watts of sunlight at the stated absorptance, and after a stated regolith infrared load delivers a net cooling flux of 267 watts per square metre, so a 10 kilowatt cooling duty needs 37 square metres. Sizing follows from computed thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: Regolith Berm Shielding for a Surface Habitat Sized Against Solar Particle Events and Galactic Cosmic Rays
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes regolith berm shielding for a reference surface habitat: an areal density of 36 grams per square centimetre, a thickness of 0.24 metres at the stated bulk density, reduces a solar particle event dose proxy by a factor of 20, while the same berm reduces a galactic cosmic ray dose proxy by only a factor of 2.22. Covering 245 square metres requires 59 cubic metres, about 88 tonnes, of regolith.

name: Solar-Sintered Regolith Roads and Landing Pads Built with a Concentrated Solar Furnace
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes solar sintering of a 400 square metre landing pad and road surface: fusing a 5 centimetre layer requires heating 30 tonnes of regolith, an energy of 33.7 gigajoules, which a 100 kilowatt solar furnace delivers in 9.4 useful solar days, a production rate near 43 square metres per day. Sizing follows from computed thermal and regolith budgets derived in the study.

name: Sulfur-Bound Regolith Concrete for Unpressurised Lunar Structures Without Process Water
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study sizes sulfur-bound regolith concrete for a reference unpressurised shell of 18 cubic metres: the structure masses 36 tonnes, of which 12.6 tonnes is sulfur binder, and melting and placing the binder requires 3.02 gigajoules at the stated allowances, with no process water. Sizing follows from computed material and thermal budgets derived in the study.

name: Thermoelectric Harvesting from the Lunar Day-Night Subsurface Temperature Gradient: A Bounded Assessment
territory: Lunar Surface Power, Thermal and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This study assesses thermoelectric harvesting from the shallow subsurface temperature gradient and finds it weak: at a device efficiency of 4.47 percent across the stated gradient, heat conduction supplies 0.80 watts per square metre and electrical output is 36 milliwatts per square metre, or 3.6 watts from 100 square metres. The Carnot factor for the stated temperatures is 23.5 percent.

name: A Capillary Heat-Pipe Network for Moving Waste Heat on a Mars Base: Two-Phase Transport Sizing
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on capillary-driven two-phase heat-pipe transport using a wick and a working fluid. A network of water and ammonia heat pipes linking heat sources inside a habitat to external radiators.

name: A Conductive Thermal Well for Extracting Water from Buried Martian Ice: Sublimation and Melt Sizing
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on conductive heating of buried ice by a heated well rod, melting and subliming ice in place for collection. A drilled thermal well, in the Rodriguez-well sense, that creates and sustains a subsurface cavity in an ice deposit.

name: A Dust-Derated Photovoltaic Array for a Mars Surface Habitat: Sizing from the Martian Solar Budget
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on photovoltaic conversion in triple-junction cells, with maximum-power-point conditioning and dust derating. A fixed-tilt triple-junction photovoltaic array feeding a conditioned direct-current bus for a four-person habitat.

name: A Fission Stirling Power Unit for Continuous Mars Surface Electricity: Conversion and Conditioning Sizing
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on dynamic free-piston Stirling conversion of fission heat to alternating current, rectified and conditioned for a surface bus. A small fission reactor coupled to free-piston Stirling convertors delivering continuous power through dust storms and night.

name: A Microwave Kiln for Martian Regolith Bricks: Dielectric-Heating Sizing for Construction Blocks
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on volumetric dielectric (microwave) heating that sinters pressed regolith bricks from the inside outward. A microwave cavity kiln producing standardised sintered bricks for walls, berms and radiation-shield blocks.

name: A Regolith Berm Shield for a Mars Habitat: Mass-Attenuation Sizing Against Galactic Cosmic Rays and Solar Particle Events
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on passive mass attenuation of radiation in a thick layer of Martian regolith placed over and around a habitat. An excavated-regolith berm and roof layer shielding an inflatable or rigid habitat module.

name: A Static Thermoelectric Backup Generator for Mars Night and Storm Survival Loads: Seebeck Conversion Sizing
territory: Mars Surface Power, Thermal, Radiation and Construction Systems Derived from the Physics
explanation: This paper presents a sized design for a Mars surface system based on static Seebeck thermoelectric conversion from a radioisotope-free heated block using reactor waste heat as the hot source. A solid-state thermoelectric unit with no moving parts that covers survival loads when dynamic convertors are offline.
